leads.title: Latta v. Otter
leads.documents: Federal case that found Idaho's constitutional amendment and statutes denying marriage to same-sex couples unconstitutional; led to marriage equality in Idaho in October 2014 after Ninth Circuit affirmance
leads.detail: No URL visible in text. Cited as: 'A ruling in the case of Latta v. Otter on May 13, 2014, found these prohibitions unconstitutional' and 'On October 7, 2014, the Ninth Circuit upheld the district court ruling'.

leads.title: Bostock v. Clayton County
leads.documents: U.S. Supreme Court ruling that workplace discrimination on basis of sexual orientation or gender identity is sex discrimination under Title VII, protecting LGBT employees where Idaho state law has no explicit protection
leads.detail: No URL visible in text. Cited as: 'On June 15, 2020, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled in Bostock v. Clayton County, consolidated with Altitude Express, Inc. v. Zarda, and in R.G. & G.R. Harris Funeral Homes Inc. v. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission'.

leads.title: Idaho HB 509 (2020)
leads.documents: Idaho law barring transgender individuals from changing sex marker on birth certificate and prohibiting transgender athletes from competing in public school and university teams matching gender identity
leads.detail: No URL visible in text. Cited as: 'On March 30, 2020, Governor Brad Little... signed legislation (HB 509) barring transgender individuals from changing the sex marker on their birth certificate and prohibiting transgender athletes...' with preliminary effect July 1, 2020 and District Court Judge David C. Nye ruling Aug 7, 2020.

leads.title: Idaho HB 71 (2023)
leads.documents: Idaho law banning puberty blockers, hormones and surgeries for minors and making it a felony for doctors to provide gender-affirming care to children
leads.detail: No URL visible in text. Cited as: 'On April 4, 2023, Governor Brad Little signed HB 71, banning puberty blockers, hormones and surgeries for minors...'.

leads.title: Idaho HB 668 (effective July 1, 2024)
leads.documents: Severely restricts gender-affirming care if provided by state/local/county professionals, via Idaho Medicaid, or on state property including hospitals, public colleges and prisons; prevents tax deductibility
leads.detail: No URL visible in text. Cited as: 'On July 1st 2024, HB668 came into force and severely restricted gender affirming care for minors and adults within the state of Idaho.'

leads.title: 2026 Idaho bathroom felony law and U.S. District Judge Amanda Brailsford June 16 ruling
leads.documents: Makes it a felony for trans person to use bathroom/changing room not matching assigned sex in publicly owned building or private business; then limited by federal judge to allow single-stall use and multi-user use when no single-user restroom on same floor
leads.detail: No URL visible in text. Cited as: 'In March 2026, the Idaho House... passed a law making it a felony...' and 'On June 16, two weeks before the law was set to take effect, U.S. District Judge Amanda Brailsford ruled that it could not be enforced...'.

leads.title: March 2026 Idaho forced outing law
leads.documents: Requires schools, childcare providers, and medical professionals to out transgender minors to parents within three days of learning of minor's trans status
leads.detail: No URL visible in text. Cited as: 'Under state law passed in March 2026, schools, childcare providers, and medical professionals are required to out transgender minors to their parents within three days...'.

leads.title: September 2024 federal court ruling on transgender prisoner hormone therapy
leads.documents: Permits transgender prisoners in Idaho to have hormone therapy; nullifies 1997 state law banning hormone therapy for prisoners
leads.detail: No URL visible in text. Cited as: 'In September 2024, transgender prisoners within Idaho are permitted to have hormone therapy - under a court ruling by a federal judge. The 1997 law banning hormone therapy on prisoners is nullified and void.'
